What we do, and how long it takes

Times are typical for shoulder length hair and are set at your consultation. Prices are examples only and change with length, density and starting color.

  • 01

    Women’s cut

    Consultation, shampoo, cut and finish. We cut for how your hair falls dry, not only wet.

    About 1 hrExample from $85
  • 02

    Short and men’s cuts

    Scissor and clipper work, neck and edge clean-up, and a style you can repeat at home.

    About 45 minExample from $55
  • 03

    Single-process color

    One formula, root to end or root only, for gray coverage or a new all-over shade.

    About 2 hrExample from $140
  • 04

    Balayage and highlights

    Hand-painted or foiled lightening, toned to the shade you picked together.

    About 3 to 4 hrExample from $260
  • 05

    Color correction

    Uneven, banded or box-dye color brought back to something even. Done in stages when needed.

    4 hr or moreExample from $400
  • 06

    Gloss and treatment

    A semi-permanent gloss for shine and tone, or a bond-repair treatment after lightening.

    About 45 minExample from $60
  • 07

    Bridal and event hair

    A trial first, then the day-of style. Bring your veil, comb or hair pieces to the trial.

    Trial about 90 minExample from $120

    Bring to your consultation

    1. Photos of the look you wantTwo or three, and one of what you do not want.
    2. Your color historyBox dye, bleach, henna or keratin treatments, with rough dates.
    3. Your real routine and budgetHow often you can return, so the plan is one you can keep up.

    How a color visit goes, in order

    1. Consultation

      You show photos, tell us your hair history and say what you will realistically do each morning. We look at your hair in daylight and agree on a target shade.

      The plan, time and example price are set here

    2. Patch or strand test, when needed

      If your hair has been colored at home, bleached before, or you have had a past reaction, we test a small section first. Not every visit needs one.

      Adds a short step, sometimes a separate visit

    3. Formula and application

      We measure the formula for your starting level and apply it by section. Lightening and toning are separate steps because they do different jobs.

      Usually the longest part of the visit

    4. Processing and toning

      Color processes while you wait, then gets rinsed, toned and checked against the target shade in natural light.

      Time depends on the service

    5. Finish and home-care plan

      We cut or style, then tell you how often to wash, which products suit your hair, and when a refresh visit makes sense for the color you chose.

      We write your formula down for next time

    Before you ask

    How long does balayage take?

    Often three to four hours for shoulder length hair, and longer for long hair or a dark starting color. The consultation gives you a time block before you commit.

    Do I need a consultation before I book color?

    Yes. Every color service begins with a short consultation, built into the appointment. Cuts do not need a separate one.

    What affects the price?

    Length, density, how much product the formula needs, the starting color and the time the service takes. A correction costs more than a refresh because it takes more steps and more time.

    Can I bring reference photos?

    Yes, please do. Photos are the fastest way to agree on a shade. We will say whether the look is possible in one visit or needs stages.

    What if I need to change my appointment?

    Call or text the salon as early as you can. Long color appointments hold a large block of the schedule, so the salon’s change policy is shared when you request your visit.

    Tell us what you have in mind

    Send a few details and the salon replies to confirm a consultation time. The plan from the builder fills in for you.
